messages:
kevin: quick sync: proposing a probe-first fairness proxy at the edge. idea: always allow a small sampled fraction through unpenalized so we can detect warm-up vs attack. want to capture tradeoffs before I write the RFC.

maya: sounds good. key questions: how big is the probe sample, and do probes count against tenant quotas?

harry: tradeoff: probes give signal but can be abused if attacker patterns mimic probes. we should mark probes transparently (header + audit log) and have a per-tenant probe budget.

diane: ops constraint: we must avoid exploding telemetry. probe events should be aggregated on minute windows and only a few probe metrics emitted (probe_pass_rate, probe_latency, probe_cache_hit).

zack: sketch of flow: edge proxy receives request -> consult local lightweight policy -> if under steady quota accept; if above but below emergency threshold mark as soft-probe with probability p -> forward with header X-Probe:true. serving tier treats X-Probe differently (bypass short-term drop, but collect features).

kevin: config proto (very small):
```json
{"policy":"probe-first-v0","probe_rate":0.005,"per_tenant_probe_quota_per_min":10,"probe_exempt_models":["embed-lite"],"probe_expiry_secs":300}
```

maya: probe_rate 0.5% seems reasonable for PLG. for enterprise tenants we should default to 0 or require opt-in. also need a kill-switch per-tenant.

harry: on fairness scheduling: proxy should maintain a small rotating credit window per-tenant to smooth burstiness (token-bucket at edge) and a separate soft-weight for priority. that way we reduce per-request chatter with a single token check.

diane: can we reuse the existing token-bucket library? it's implemented in Rust and already hot at the edge; only gap is telemetry tags for probes.

zack: yes reuse. also propose a backpressure signal header from central allocator: X-Weight:0.6 to bias routing and reduce concurrency. proxies should honor it eventually (best-effort).

kevin: abuse detection: sampled probes feed a lightweight classifier (features: inter-arrival variance, prompt-similarity-signature, kv_cache_warmth, client_ip_entropy). classifier returns score in range [0,1] and we map to actions: <0.2 no-op, 0.2-0.6 increase drop-rate, >0.6 immediate reject + flag.

maya: classifier latency must be tiny (<50ms) or run async with action applied to subsequent requests. prefer async enrichment to avoid inflating p99.

harry: agree. async enrichment + per-tenant short memory. for immediate concerns, use simple heuristics at edge (e.g., >1000 reqs/min with low cache hit) to preemptively escalate.

telemetry-bot: emitted metrics: tenant.probe.count (m), tenant.probe.pass_rate (m), tenant.probe.latency_p95 (m), tenant.abuse.score_sampled (m). usage: aggregated per 1m.

kevin: rollout plan: 1) unit tests + local dev proxy flag. 2) 0.1% tenant canary (PLG only) with probe_rate=0.01 and async classifier. 3) monitor probe_pass_rate and false-positive complaints for 48h. 4) widen to 1% then enterprise opt-in.

diane: ops additions: add alert when probe_pass_rate drops >50% from baseline or sampled abuse_score >0.5 for >10m. also add runbook to disable probes per-tenant instantly.

zack: one more design note: probes must not consume critical KV cache quota; tag them and if cache eviction pressure high, deprioritize probes. we need a small accounting path so probes don't harm cache-sensitive tenants.

maya: client experience: document that probes exist and will not generally count as quota (unless abused). add header X-Probe-Notice in responses for transparency.

harry: caching the classifier verdict per-tenant for short TTL (e.g., 60s) reduces noise. also persist in low-cardinality store so allocator can use it in decisions.

canary-bot: scheduled canary: probe-first-proxy v0.1 -> canary cohort at 6234569000. will report hourly.

kevin: thanks team. action items: I'll draft RFC with diagrams, config schema, and telemetry list. @diane please add runbook snippets. meet Thurs 10am to finalize before canary.
